acceptance: Release-v2 probe queue/start/completion states have bounded fake-clock coverage; child failure/cancellation still fails and never-started runs terminate with a distinct diagnosis.
Watchdog empty-read cause is identified and regression-tested with injected timing; 200 sequential repetitions on an idle host via heavy-run pass.

Trunk run 43910721968 failing test is identified and fixed here or linked to a named owning item; duration/baseline work is explicitly routed to ci-fast-duration-gate-rerun-and-baseline-drift-20261113.
External artifact-service failure has evidence and recovery disposition without asserting an unproven repository bug.
context:
Filed 2026-11-16 while landing the TPC-DI release-gate restore and two small follow-ups: identified during that work and not addressed.

2026-11-16/17 recurrences: release-v2 probe timed out four times on PR #4251 ('did not finish within 1177s' and once 181s; once 'no release-v2.yml run appeared') with 20-35 runs queued, passing on the fifth attempt; PR #4274 needed a core re-run; develop trunk run 43910721968 failed in medium-test shard 0 at PR #4280 and passed on a failed-jobs re-run, which blocked arming for about a day. Failing test id in that shard not recorded.

2026-11-17 review fix: the earlier acceptance 'passes 200 consecutive runs under load' was replaced, because meeting it needs deliberate host load, which caused the 2026-11-13 spin-loop leak. Decision gate: the probe-wait and duration-gate options are chosen by the implementer with reasons; anything that changes a required check or its pass threshold needs owner approval first. Item guardrails: never start deliberate CPU or memory load; no change to required checks or rulesets without owner approval; do not raise timeouts without measuring queue time. Verification rubric: pass = all three acceptance points with log excerpts or run ids. Fail = a 'fix' that only adds retries or longer waits without a recorded cause.

2026-11-17 TODO review: clarified decision gates, observable pass/fail rubric and safety boundaries. Existing historical evidence is retained; this is tracker planning only, not implementation, spend, publication or closeout approval.

Owner decision 2026-11-17: release-v2 probe gets a queue-aware wait: the run time limit starts when the dispatched run starts, a separate bounded queue limit applies, and 'still queued' is a distinct message. The check stays required with the same pass rule. This approval covers that change only.

2026-11-17 owner decision: no threshold changes; improve messages and separate queue time from run time in the release-v2 probe.

2026-11-17: implemented in #4322 (head 06437f9a51). The release-v2 probe now distinguishes queue time from run time; on this PR it failed twice for backlog and its new message correctly reported "still queued after 1181.01s ... never began running; ... not a release-v2 failure". 200 sequential watchdog-test repetitions passed; the trunk 43910721968 failure is identified (details in the PR). Under the no-threshold-change decision the 1200 s budget is unchanged; if backlog timeouts keep recurring, a longer probe wait needs an owner decision.

2026-11-18 recurrence: BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4292 (head 94552d334, review SHIP, all other required checks green) cannot be armed because `release-v2 probe` failed 4 times with 'run N did not finish within ~1175s'. The queue held 115-149 queued runs with about 5 in progress between 00:11 and 02:00 UTC on 2026-11-18 (mostly CI and review-verdict runs for other PRs, plus the 0.5.2rc2 Release v2 push run), so the dispatched Release v2 runs never started within the probe's window. The probe attempts' own queued Release v2 runs (44202347417, 44202364922, 44202386464) were cancelled to stop adding load.

2026-11-18 root cause (5 whys, from #4292 probe run 44176425907 attempt 6 and its dispatched run 44311910625):
1. The probe fails because its first dispatched Release v2 run does not finish within the 1200 s budget passed by release-v2-probe.yml (`--timeout-seconds 1200`, measured by release_probe_launch.py's wait_for from dispatch, inside a 30-minute job).
2. The run does not finish because nearly all of its time is spent waiting for runners, not working: admit 13:15:46-13:17:06, then UAT evidence reuse waited 1 min, install 3.12 waited 2.5 min, probe reused UAT evidence waited 5.5 min, and release UAT gate was queued from 13:26:21 until the cancel at 13:35:44 with 0 steps executed (the job never got a runner). The work itself takes about 4 minutes; successful probe runs on quieter days took 11-17 min end to end.
3. Jobs wait because the org is on the GitHub Free plan (`plan=free`), which caps concurrent jobs for the whole org (GitHub documents 20, 5 of them macOS). Each Release v2 run has about 7 dependent jobs, and each re-enters the job queue when its predecessor finishes, so a run's latency is roughly (dependent jobs) x (job-queue wait).
4. The job queue is saturated because every PR push fans out into far more jobs than the cap: a CI run has about 30 jobs, and each probe dispatches 3 Release v2 runs at once. Probes run on every PR touching a PROBED_PATHS file (including trunk.yml and scripts/release_*.py). On 2026-11-17/18, 95 probe dispatches ran for 7 branches and 90 were cancelled (timeout or superseded); 21 Release v2 runs were dispatched in the two minutes 13:15-13:17 on 2026-11-18 alone. Each rerun of a timed-out probe adds 3 more runs, so retries deepen the congestion they are waiting out. The repository-level queued-run count is a poor signal: it fell to 15 (all ghost runs from 2026-11-11 that never start) while jobs still waited minutes for runners.
5. The probe's pass criterion is a fixed wall-clock deadline that includes queue time it neither controls nor measures, calibrated when the org was quiet, with no admission control or concurrency cap on the probes themselves. Under normal multi-agent load its outcome measures runner availability, not the release workflow.
Fix directions (owner to choose): measure the budget from each job's start (or from run start plus a queue allowance), not from dispatch; dispatch the 3 variants serially or cap concurrent probe runs repo-wide with one concurrency group; skip or cancel probe work for heads that are superseded; add runner capacity (paid plan or larger/self-hosted runners). Raising the timeout alone would just make each failure slower.

2026-11-18 evaluation of fixes with the owner's decisions:
- Starting the probe clock when the dispatched run starts (the release_probe_launch.py change in #4322) does not fix it: a run is in_progress once its first job starts, while its later dependent jobs each still wait for runners (1-9 min each on 44311910625), and the probe job itself polls inside a runner with a 30-minute job timeout while dispatched runs took 49-189 min overnight. It improves the error message only; #4322's own probe failed the same way.
- Serialising variants or capping probe concurrency makes it worse: probe-dispatched runs are under 10% of runner time (about 400 of ~9,000 runner-minutes over 24 h; CI about 7,400; the v0.5.2rc2 release about 1,286 in 18 UAT shards held for about 3 h) and serialising triples each probe's exposure to queueing.
- Owner-approved fix (P1): make the probe asynchronous. The probe job dispatches the 3 variants, creates the required `release-v2 probe` check run in progress and exits; a workflow_run-triggered verdict workflow completes it when all 3 variants finish (success only if all succeeded). No deadline and no held runner; congestion delays the check but cannot fail it.
- Owner-approved (P2): cap UAT matrix parallelism (max-parallel 4/2/3 for stages 1/2/3 in release-v2.yml and trunk-uat.yml, at most 9 of the Free plan's 20 concurrent jobs); decide on GitHub Team after a week of measurement.
- So the release_probe_launch.py change in #4322 becomes obsolete under P1; its owner can drop it from #4322 and keep the other changes.
- 15 runs created 2026-11-11 stay queued forever and cannot be cancelled (`gh run cancel`: 'completed'; force-cancel: 409 'has not been queued yet'); they inflate the repository's queued-run count and should not be used as a congestion signal.

Owner decision 2026-11-18: release-v2 probe queue time is not counted. The probe waits for its dispatched run to start for as long as the job allows (timeout-minutes 360, the hosted maximum) and limits only start-to-finish (1500 s); failure, cancellation or timeout of a started run still fails the check. Applied on PR #4311 after three probe runs failed the 1200 s queue limit with 97 runs queued and only 3 jobs running org-wide (Free plan, no GitHub incident).

2026-11-18: the asynchronous probe is https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4354 (head 7f08377a67, review SHIP; all 3 variant runs 44372525120, 44372549614, 44372571841 succeeded; check run app id 15368 confirmed). It cannot complete its own `release-v2 probe` check because the verdict workflow runs only from develop and a personal token gets HTTP 403 'You must authenticate via a GitHub App' when completing an Actions-app check run. Open PR #4311 (fix/pr-arm-transient-reads) also changes the probe (queue-aware deadline) and conflicts with #4354; a comment on #4311 recommends dropping its probe files.

2026-11-18 evidence: PR #4334 CI run 44214765170 job 134518754187 `TPC-H binary framing (windows-latest)` failed in 'Install dependencies': `Failed to download datafusion==55.0.0 ... network timeout. Try increasing UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT (current value: 30s)`; `core` then failed only on that result, and rerun-failed-jobs passed. Candidate change for this item: give Windows `uv sync` steps a longer UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT or retries. Any CI timeout change still needs the owner's approval per this item's guardrails. Verification: no 'network timeout' install failure on the Windows jobs over 14 days of ci.yml runs after the change.

2026-11-18 new occurrence: BenchBox #4347 (docs-only, CI run 44312861045 attempt 1). `TPC-H binary framing (macos-latest)` started 13:22:29Z and was cancelled 13:45:50Z with zero steps run (timeout-minutes 15), so `core` reported `tpch-binary-framing=abandoned (required for this change)` and `make pr-arm` refused. A full `make pr-rerun` passed. Why a docs-only change ran the framing jobs at all is filed separately as docs-agent-edit-without-reader-escalates-full-heavy-tier-20261118; this item owns the runner-side cancellation and how `core` classifies a job that never ran a step.

2026-11-18: fixed by https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4354, merged as cf2e0e0 (head 61b8d86). The probe is now asynchronous: the `release-v2 probe dispatch` job dispatches the 3 variants, creates the `release-v2 probe` check in progress (app id 15368) and exits in under a minute; `release-v2-probe-verdict.yml` (workflow_run) completes it when all 3 finish, success only if all succeeded. Re-running the dispatch job after the runs finish reconciles a check whose workflow_run event was missed; that is how #4354 completed its own check (rerun 23:06:35Z, check success 23:06:54Z). The UAT matrices in release-v2.yml and trunk-uat.yml are capped at max-parallel 4/2/3. Remaining: confirm the verdict workflow fires by itself on the next probed PR (#4292), and measure runner demand for a week before deciding on GitHub Team.

2026-11-19: first live use on #4292 (merged f399048). The probe did not falsely fail, but `release-v2-probe-verdict.yml` never fired (zero runs): variant runs dispatched with GITHUB_TOKEN have actor github-actions[bot], and GitHub raises no workflow_run event for them. Re-running the dispatch job reconciled the check (success, 01:47:54Z, app 15368). Owner chose the fix: a final probe-report job in release-v2.yml probe mode that completes the check, judging each variant by its substantive jobs to avoid the finish-together race; the dead verdict workflow is to be removed. In progress on branch fix/release-probe-inline-verdict.

2026-11-19: verdict gap fixed by https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4379, merged as 3d7619e (head e3b8a02). Each probe-mode release-v2.yml run has a final `probe report` job (needs all 14 jobs, if: always() in probe mode only, checks: write) that completes `release-v2 probe`, judging the current run from `needs` and other runs from their substantive jobs, so variants that finish together cannot leave it stuck. release_probe_graph.py enforces the report job's shape; the dead release-v2-probe-verdict.yml is deleted. Live proof with no manual step: head c73dc812 check success at 03:50:16Z, head e3b8a02a check success at 04:11:01Z, both app 15368. Only step left: about 2026-11-26, measure a week of runner demand with the UAT caps (4/2/3) and give the owner the GitHub Team decision.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-16, with 40 to 58 workflow runs queued, three pull requests that touched only tests or deleted code needed five manual re-runs to merge:
- `release-v2 probe` failed three times on BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4257 with 'run <id> did not finish within 1177s': the probe dispatches a Release v2 run and waits about 20 minutes, and the dispatched run stayed queued behind the backlog.
- The fast-tier duration gate failed on #4258 with summed ratio 1.381 and delta +728.4 s, on a change that only removes code and tests. Re-running the failed job repeated the same numbers because it re-reads the recorded durations; only a full re-run of the workflow re-measured, and that passed.
- `tests/unit/utils/test_heavy_watchdog.py::test_run_guard_subprocess_stops_a_runaway_command_with_the_watchdog_status` failed once in medium-test shard 2 on #4257 with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''` and passed on re-run.
A fourth failure was GitHub's artifact service ('Failed to FinalizeArtifact'), which is external.

## Change
- Probe: wait for the dispatched run to start before starting the completion clock, or scale the wait with queue depth.
- Duration gate: say in the failure message that a job re-run reuses the measurement and a full re-run is needed; consider normalising for runner load.
- Watchdog test: find the empty-string read (probably a pid or status file read before it is written) and make it wait for the value.

## Guardrails
- Do not loosen the duration thresholds to hide real regressions.
- The probe must still fail when the dispatched run fails.

## Decision gates
Separate proven failure classes: release-v2 queue wait and watchdog empty-string race remain here; duration-gate measurement/baseline work is owned by ci-fast-duration-gate-rerun-and-baseline-drift-20261113. Identify the test behind trunk run 43910721968 rather than assuming it is the same race. GitHub FinalizeArtifact HTML/JSON failure is external evidence, not proof of a code defect. Implementer may choose bounded queue/run reporting; required-check or threshold changes require owner approval.

## Verification rubric
Pass: fake-clock workflow cases cover delayed dispatch visibility, queued beyond execution budget, starts then succeeds/fails/cancels, and never starts (finite total wait). A watchdog test injects the identified race deterministically and passes 200 sequential idle-host repetitions under heavy-run. Link the trunk failure test/disposition and duration-owner item. Record artifact-service failure with run provenance and safe existing rerun guidance; add product retry only if evidence justifies it.

## Additional guardrails
No deliberate CPU/memory load or spin loops. No indefinitely waiting queued runs, inflated timeout without evidence, retry storm, swallowed child failure or required-check bypass. Changes in duration thresholds stay with their owner item.
